theSecondMechanism.whyNamed: The dispatch asks for a second mechanism that would produce the same observation, and here it is load-bearing -- it changes the fix class.
theSecondMechanism.fact1: The bake's INPUT is the atoms store, not the ledger. nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts:3 -- 'F-06 Tier-1 facet bake from conformant-v1 hauska_mcp atoms (publish lane)'; its read is `SELECT entity_id, body FROM atoms WHERE ...` (line 354), against ATOMS_DATABASE_URL.
theSecondMechanism.fact2: The cell writers for these rails mint no atom. hauska-factory/src/jobs/parcel-envelope-cells.mjs writes parcel_record_cell only (UPDATE parcel_record_cell prc, line 205; its own 'Bypasses' line names 'a hand UPDATE/INSERT on parcel_record_cell' as the only other writer), and parcel-setback-cells.mjs is the same shape.
theSecondMechanism.consequence: For the envelope and setback rails a cell write is not, by itself, an input the bake can read. A trigger that enqueued a parcel on a cell write would enqueue it and re-materialize the SAME atoms -- the rasterised payload would not change. So 'add a trigger to the bake' is necessary but not sufficient for these rails, and the narrower honest statement of the defect is: the ledger is the declared serving path for these rails (2026-09-11 ruling, 'THE LEDGER IS THE SERVING PATH, ATOMS ARE CANONICAL'), and place_layer_snapshots is a second, hand-refreshed copy that the customer surface still reads for baseFacts.
theSecondMechanism.notMeasured: Whether an atom for maxHeightFt exists for 48209:100226 at all. A per-parcel atoms lookup by entity_id TIMES OUT (~120 s statement timeout) with no usable index for that predicate, so this lane reports it as NOT MEASURED rather than inferring it. This is the single most useful thing the next seat can measure, and it decides whether the fix is 'trigger the bake' or 'point these rails at the ledger'.
theSecondMechanism.theFixClassThatActuallyApplies: (b) structural, per the dispatch's own trap: a faster schedule narrows the window without closing it, and costs a whole-county rewrite per tick (194,538 Hays rows). The two candidate fixes are (1) a per-parcel enqueue from the cell write into the bake, which first needs the atom question above answered, or (2) serve these rails from the ledger for the six counties, which is what the 2026-09-11 ruling already says is law. This lane proposes neither as shipped work; it names the class.
